account:
Today has seemed unusually light on actual municipal business, with several hints of preparations that nobody has clearly explained to me. At my town accounts appointment, the secretary said no figures had been supplied. The builder instead asked me to inspect the great hall lighting tomorrow at 18:00, saying eight lanterns are installed and that no accounts or approvals are needed, just my opinion. I agreed, but the secretary subsequently asked for approval again, so I have just explicitly repeated my approval and asked whether it is recorded. I have not yet heard a reply.

At three o'clock I visited my neighbour's dockside cottage for tea. The neighbour reported chatter about lights or decorations at the bakery, but had not seen them and said the baker knew of no celebration. The neighbour later identified Townsfolk 02 as the source, including an odd reference to a bridge or port change, and cautioned that the report was unreliable. I also heard the builder shouting in the distance during tea, but could not understand the words.

The concrete unusual development is the installation of eight great hall lanterns and tomorrow evening's inspection invitation. The builder and secretary are involved in arranging that visit. Townsfolk 02 is associated with the unverified bakery story; my neighbour merely relayed it. These details make me wonder whether a gathering or some other preparation is taking place without my knowledge, perhaps connected to the great hall, but I have no evidence of its purpose or of a connection to the bakery. The stated purpose remains an ordinary lighting inspection. For now I am back at the office seeking correspondence, pending business, and confirmation of tomorrow's appointment; I am due home at 19:00.
